citation.source: Choi & Okos (1986) predictive food-thermal-property model — see potato.json's identical citation

metadata.notes: Whole egg-in-shell, modeled solid like potato.json even though its contents are liquid until cracked — same 'intact object until an action changes it' convention. statePrerequisites.peel mirrors potato.json's statePrerequisites.cut: you peel a BOILED egg's shell, not a raw one, so peel presupposes state 'boiled' — reuses the existing peel action rather than inventing a new verb. thermophysical values are typical whole-egg literature approximations, not measured. producedByproducts (egg_shell) is the flat fallback both PEEL and SEPARATE would otherwise use; byproductsByAction overrides SEPARATE (adds egg_yolk + egg_white) and CRACK (adds egg_cracked instead — yolk and white kept together, see data/actions/crack.json) since both also destroysTarget. POACH deliberately does NOT go through crack/separate first — like FRY it glosses over shell removal for a raw whole egg cooked directly (see data/actions/poach.json). criticalControlPointsByAction (data/ccps/egg_cooking.json, src/thermal.ts) ties FRY/POACH/BOIL on this whole egg to the same Salmonella threshold FRY/SCRAMBLE carry on egg_cracked.json below — the risk belongs to the egg, not to whichever verb happens to cook it. Not on PEEL/SALT/SEPARATE/CRACK (no thermal step, PASTEURIZE aside).
metadata.pasteurizeNote: isPasteurizable + criticalControlPointsByAction.pasteurize (data/ccps/egg_pasteurization_raw.json, advisoryOnly: false — a hard reject, not a warning, unlike egg_cooking.json's runny-yolk case). Added for the alioli-with-egg-yolk case: any recipe using raw separated yolk (data/entities/egg_yolk.json) should pasteurize the whole egg here BEFORE separating — see data/actions/separate.json's byproduct spawning, which now inherits the 'pasteurized' tag onto egg_yolk/egg_white (engine.ts tag-propagation fix) rather than silently dropping it.
metadata.shockNote: isShockable + statePrerequisites.shock: 'boiled' — see data/actions/shock.json's carryoverCookingNote for why this matters more than it looks like it should: BOIL's durationSeconds doesn't fully determine final doneness on its own, residual heat keeps cooking the egg after it leaves the pot until this action (or slow, uncontrolled ambient cooling) stops it.
metadata.seasoningNote: pepper/chili added 2026-08-13 alongside salt — see potato.json's identical seasoningNote.
metadata.simmerNote: SIMMER (data/actions/simmer.json) added 2026-08-13, isSimmerable alongside isBoilable, reaching the SAME 'boiled' state BOIL does (see simmer.json's sharedTransformedStateNote) — statePrerequisites.peel/shock above ('boiled') therefore work unchanged for an egg cooked via SIMMER, no separate wiring needed. criticalControlPointsByAction.simmer reuses 'egg_cooking', the identical CCP boil/fry/poach already reference: Salmonella kill-time is a function of internal temperature and hold duration, not of how turbulently the water moved to get there. The real reason this verb exists for egg specifically: a rolling boil's turbulence is a common, preventable CAUSE of shell cracking during cooking — see crackContainmentNote below for what to do once a crack has already happened; this is the complementary, more-preventable half of the same real risk.
metadata.freshnessNote: 'fresh'/'aged' added 2026-08-13, directly answering 'getting the perfect egg shape in the pan' — a real, cited, currently-unmodeled factor. As an egg ages, the thick albumen's ovomucin protein network (which traps water and gives fresh white its gel-like body) progressively breaks down — see MDPI, "Non-Destructive Evaluation of Physicochemical Properties for Egg Freshness: A Review" (2024), https://www.mdpi.com/2077-0472/14/11/2049, and the albumen-viscosity study it cites, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0032579119424632 — both verified via direct lookup 2026-08-13. Practical effect FRY actually cares about: a very fresh egg cracked into a pan holds its shape and stands tall; an older egg's white has measurably lower viscosity and spreads flat and ragged immediately — the real mechanism behind 'getting the perfect egg shape,' not pan temperature or technique alone. Also the more credible explanation (see crackContainmentNote below) for why older eggs peel more easily after boiling. Deliberately NOT wired to any action: this repo has no concept of elapsed real-world time and no 'AGE' verb (nor should there be one) — 'fresh'/'aged' can only be set as a starting tag on a specific egg instance in a recipe's initialInventory (RecipeInstanceSchema.tags), the same mechanism already used for any other pre-existing property a recipe author asserts about their starting ingredients, not something applyAction ever derives or changes.
metadata.crackContainmentNote: Real, commonly-cited technique — salt (or vinegar) added to the BOILING WATER before/while boiling an egg, distinct from and NOT modeled via data/actions/salt.json's SALT verb, on purpose: SALT targets a food entity and adds tag 'salted' for a seasoning/flavor reason (osmosis, browning — see salt.json's timingNote); salting the water an egg boils in is NOT primarily about flavor at all — the shell/white barely absorb it during a ~10 minute boil, unlike a porous food like pasta. The real, causal mechanism is different: if the shell cracks during boiling, salt (and separately, vinegar/acid) speeds coagulation of the leaking egg white on contact with the salted water, sealing the crack faster and containing the mess, rather than letting white stream out into plain water. A commonly-repeated SECOND claim — that salting the water makes peeling easier — is NOT included here with the same confidence: evidence for it is mixed/disputed; easier peeling is more reliably explained by egg freshness (older eggs peel easier as the shell's inner membrane separates more with age/CO2 loss — see freshnessNote above, now backed by a real citation, added 2026-08-13) and by shock.json's ice-bath shock, not by water salinity. Deliberately not built as a new action/mechanism this session (would need water.json to accept an additive for a non-seasoning, non-isSeasonable reason — a genuinely different concept SALT's isSeasonable/isSeasoning capabilities don't fit) — named precisely as a real, correctly out-of-scope gap rather than forced into the wrong verb just to have something.
metadata.crackPreventionNote: The complement to crackContainmentNote above — what to do to AVOID a crack happening at all, not what to do once one has. Added 2026-08-14, directly answering 'the robot has to try not to break the egg.' Three genuinely different real moments/mechanisms, each covered by a different, already-existing piece of this vocabulary rather than one new blanket 'don't crack it' flag: (1) entry into the water — boil.json/simmer.json's placementMethod (mechanical impact from dropping) and startMethod (thermal shock from boiling_start vs. cold_start — startMethodNote is explicit that these trade off against EGG_BOIL_DONENESS's own boiling_start assumption, an unresolved real tension, not silently picked for the user); (2) during cooking — simmerNote above, turbulence from a rolling boil knocking the egg around, SIMMER's whole reason for existing; (3) after cooking — shock.json's ice bath, arresting carryover cooking, not a crack-prevention mechanism at all (named here only to be complete about what happens at each stage). No single 'crack risk' number or probability exists anywhere in this repo for any of the three — informational technique parameters only, matching this vocabulary's standing honesty limit on categorical parameters (fry.json's heatLevel/agitation notes state the same limit).
metadata.invalidTransitionsNote: Closed 2026-08-15, ROADMAP.md Phase 4. Egg is the concrete proof that invalidTransitions had to be keyed PER ENTITY, not one global map (see ingredient.ts's field doc comment): potato.json forbids boiled -> peeled ('peel before you boil, per its own convention'), while egg's own statePrerequisites.peel: 'boiled' REQUIRES the exact opposite order (boil before you peel) — a real egg is peeled AFTER boiling, always. A shared global matrix keyed by bare state names could not express both rules at once without one silently overriding the other; per-entity keying holds both correctly, with zero conflict. Forward chain (boiled -> peeled -> cut/sliced-diced-chopped) is intentionally NOT restricted here — that's what statePrerequisites already governs; this field only blocks the REVERSE (a cut, fried, or poached egg reverting to peeled/boiled/raw, which is what's actually physically impossible).
metadata.cutNote: isChoppable + statePrerequisites.cut: 'peeled' added 2026-08-14, directly answering 'after boiled you can cut in blocks, add salt, use it in a salad' — egg salad prep, real and common. Requires 'peeled' specifically (not potato.json's ['washed','peeled'] either/or) because there's no skin-on-egg equivalent of a skin-on potato wedge — you cut a peeled boiled egg or you don't cut it at all; cutting through shell isn't a real technique this vocabulary needs to represent. possibleStates deliberately lists only 'sliced'/'diced'/'chopped' out of cut.json's full five-value shape enum, NOT 'julienne'/'minced' too — sliced (egg slicer, rounds/wedges — the classic salad-topping cut) and diced/chopped (egg salad itself) are real, common results for a cut boiled egg; julienne (thin matchsticks, for fibrous/firm vegetables) and mincing an egg aren't real techniques anyone actually does. Named honestly rather than left implied: this is possibleStates being an accurate DECLARATION, not an ENFORCEMENT — cut.json's own 'shape' parameter is one shared enum across every isChoppable entity with no per-entity restriction mechanism, so nothing in engine.ts actually stops a caller from requesting 'julienne' or 'minced' egg today; building that per-entity-per-parameter-value restriction would be new, unscoped engine architecture (same category as the deferred SEASON-generalization gap above), not something this addition attempts. No byproduct spawns from cutting an egg (outputs.spawnsTargetByproducts: false, matching cut.json's own default) — unlike potato, there's no discarded piece (peel) left over once the egg is already peeled; every gram of the peeled egg ends up in the cut pieces.
metadata.extractionAndRestingNote: Two real steps this vocabulary still does NOT represent, named honestly rather than glossed over, surfaced directly by 'how do you get the egg out of the boiling water — do you wait, or shock, before peeling': (1) REMOVING the egg from the pot. Nothing in this repo tracks which tool/place an ingredient instance currently occupies (ROADMAP.md's 'heat as a shared, time-varying place' entry, 2026-08-14 update — the physics half closed via src/place.ts, the co-location half explicitly still open) — BOIL, SHOCK, and PEEL just run in sequence with no representation of the egg ever being 'in' the pot at all, so there is nothing to formally take it OUT of. (2) WAITING (ambient cooling) as an alternative to SHOCK. Both are real, valid paths already representable at the SEQUENCING level without any new mechanism, which is the actual answer to 'do you wait or shock': statePrerequisites.peel only requires 'boiled', not the 'shocked' tag — SHOCK is genuinely optional, so BOIL -> PEEL (implicitly: however the egg got out of the pot, then left to cool however long before peeling) and BOIL -> SHOCK -> PEEL (controlled ice-bath, immediately) are BOTH valid sequences today, matching real kitchen practice. What's NOT modeled is 'waiting' itself as a distinct, named step with a duration — there's no REST/COOL verb (ROADMAP.md's 'More common technique verbs' list already names REST as open: 'post-cook carryover exists narrowly for egg via SHOCK, not generally') — so an uncontrolled ambient wait is invisible to this model in exactly the way SHOCK's carryoverCookingNote already warns about: skip SHOCK and let the egg sit, and the SAME durationSeconds that gave one result can give a firmer one depending entirely on how long an unmodeled wait actually lasted.
